name: spacer
description: Declarative whitespace block bound to `--space-*` tokens. Use when sibling spacing can't come from a parent's `gap`.

props.name: size
props.description: Spacing token (xs=0.25rem, sm=0.5rem, md=1rem, lg=2rem, xl=4rem). Bound to `--space-*`.

props.name: axis
props.description: Which axis to expand. Vertical = height; horizontal = width; both = square.

variants.name: axis
variants.description: Which axis the spacer extends along.

values.description: Fixed width, 1px height — for flex rows.
Square block — rare; usually pick one axis.

examples.title: Vertical breathing room
examples.description: Push two sections apart inside a parent that doesn't manage gap.

examples.title: Horizontal flex spacer
examples.description: Push siblings to opposite ends of a flex row.

ai.whenToUse: Use as an explicit whitespace primitive when you can't (or don't want to) use `gap` on the parent — typically: pushing siblings apart inside a flex row that already has gap-0, or inserting one-off vertical breathing room between top-level sections that aren't wrapped in a Stack.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use Spacer when a `Stack` or `Cluster` parent's `gap` would do the same thing — that scales better and keeps the spacing concern with the layout primitive. Don't use Spacer to flush content to one edge of a flex container — use `ml-auto` / `justify-between` directly.
commonMistakes: Using `<Spacer />` between every child in a Stack — just set the Stack's `gap` instead
Using `axis="both"` and getting a square block where you wanted a line — `both` is rare, usually you want vertical or horizontal
Setting size="lg" on a horizontal spacer and getting nothing visible because the parent isn't a flex row — Spacer reserves space, it doesn't push siblings on its own
ai.accessibilityNotes: Spacer is `aria-hidden="true"` — screen readers skip it. Don't use a Spacer where a `Separator` would convey meaning (a thematic break should be `Separator`, not `Spacer`).
